questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Health and disease; pathogens and parasites
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-infectious disease?

solution.key_concept: Infectious diseases pass from one person to another. Non-infectious diseases do not.
steps: Typhoid, malaria and AIDS spread from person to person, so they are infectious.
Cancer does not pass from one person to another, so it is non-infectious.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Cancer
solution.why_not_others: Typhoid (bacterial), malaria (protozoan) and AIDS (viral) are all infectious diseases.
solution.common_trap: Assuming any major cause of death must be infectious. Cancer is a major non-infectious cause of death.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Health and disease; pathogens and parasites
questions.question: A pathogen that enters the body through contaminated food and settles in the intestine must be adapted to the host environment. Which adaptation is essential for it?
options: Resistance to stomach acid and digestive enzymes
Ability to form gametocytes in RBCs

solution.key_concept: A pathogen must adapt to its environment within the host.
steps: A food-borne pathogen passes through the stomach before it reaches the intestine.
On the way, it meets stomach acid and digestive enzymes.
Intestinal pathogens therefore resist stomach acid and digestive enzymes.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Resistance to stomach acid and digestive enzymes
solution.why_not_others: UV resistance has nothing to do with life inside the gut. Gametocyte formation and haemozoin release are features of Plasmodium in the blood, not of intestinal pathogens.
solution.common_trap: Picking a familiar pathogen feature, such as haemozoin, that has nothing to do with the intestinal environment.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Health and disease; pathogens and parasites
questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only groups of pathogens?

solution.key_concept: Pathogens are disease-causing organisms: bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans and helminths.
steps: Check each list against the five pathogen groups.
Mosquitoes and houseflies are vectors, mast cells are host cells, and carcinogens are cancer-causing agents.
Only bacteria, fungi, protozoans and helminths are all pathogen groups.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Bacteria, fungi, protozoans, helminths
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 includes vectors. Option 2 includes mast cells, which are host immune cells. Option 4 includes carcinogens, which are not organisms.
solution.common_trap: Confusing vectors, which carry pathogens, with the pathogens themselves.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Health and disease; pathogens and parasites
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Health is defined simply as the absence of disease.
statements.R: Health depends on genetic factors, infections, lifestyle and a balanced mind.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being, not merely the absence of disease.
steps: A is false: health is more than the absence of disease.
R is true: genetic factors, infections, lifestyle and a balanced mind all affect health.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Accepting the everyday meaning of health, absence of disease, instead of the full definition.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Health and disease; pathogens and parasites
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: To cause disease, a pathogen must enter the body, multiply and interfere with the normal functions of the host.
statements.II: Houseflies act as mechanical carriers of Entamoeba histolytica, which is an example of disease spread through vectors.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Pathogens enter, multiply and disrupt host function. Vectors such as houseflies help spread disease.
steps: Statement I matches the requirements a pathogen must meet to cause disease, so it is correct.
Houseflies are mechanical carriers of Entamoeba histolytica, and houseflies are listed as vectors, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are factually correct, so options that reject either one are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Thinking only mosquitoes count as vectors. Houseflies also spread pathogens.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human diseases: malaria, filariasis, ascariasis, typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, amoebiasis, ringworm, dengue, chikungunya
questions.question: Common cold is caused by

solution.key_concept: Common cold is a viral infection of the nose and respiratory passage.
steps: Rhinoviruses infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs.
Common cold lasts 3-7 days.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Rhinoviruses
solution.why_not_others: Plasmodium causes malaria, Salmonella typhi causes typhoid, and Streptococcus pneumoniae causes pneumonia.
solution.common_trap: Confusing common cold with pneumonia, which is bacterial and infects the alveoli.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human diseases: malaria, filariasis, ascariasis, typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, amoebiasis, ringworm, dengue, chikungunya
questions.question: Which event in the life cycle of Plasmodium takes place in the human body?
options: Asexual multiplication in liver cells and RBCs
Storage of sporozoites in salivary glands
Development of the zygote in the gut

solution.key_concept: Humans are the intermediate host of Plasmodium, where it reproduces only asexually.
steps: Sporozoites enter humans through the bite of a female Anopheles mosquito.
They multiply asexually, first in liver cells and then in RBCs.
Fertilisation, development and storage of sporozoites in the salivary glands all occur in the mosquito.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Asexual multiplication in liver cells and RBCs
solution.why_not_others: Fertilisation, zygote development and sporozoite storage in the salivary glands all happen inside the mosquito, which is the definitive host.
solution.common_trap: Thinking Plasmodium reproduces sexually in human RBCs because gametocytes form there.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human diseases: malaria, filariasis, ascariasis, typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, amoebiasis, ringworm, dengue, chikungunya
questions.question: A patient has a sustained high fever of 39-40 degrees C, weakness, stomach pain, constipation, headache and loss of appetite. Which test would confirm the most likely disease?

solution.key_concept: These symptoms are typical of typhoid, which is confirmed by the Widal test.
steps: A sustained 39-40 degrees C fever with constipation, stomach pain and loss of appetite points to typhoid, caused by Salmonella typhi.
Typhoid is confirmed by the Widal test.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Widal test
solution.why_not_others: Bone marrow tests are used for leukaemia. MRI and histopathological study are used in cancer detection.
solution.common_trap: Picking a general diagnostic method instead of the specific test for typhoid.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human diseases: malaria, filariasis, ascariasis, typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, amoebiasis, ringworm, dengue, chikungunya
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each disease is caused by a specific pathogen.
steps: Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti (A-III).
Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica (B-IV).
Ringworm is caused by Trichophyton (C-I).
Pneumonia is caused by Haemophilus influenzae (D-II).
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the pathogens of amoebiasis and ringworm. Option 2 swaps the pathogens of filariasis and amoebiasis. Option 3 swaps the pathogens of ringworm and pneumonia.
solution.common_trap: Assigning the fungal genus Trichophyton to a protozoan disease, or Entamoeba to a skin infection.
solution.time_saving_tip: Once A-III and B-IV are fixed, only option 3 and option 4 remain; C-I then settles the answer.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Human diseases: malaria, filariasis, ascariasis, typhoid, pneumonia, common cold, amoebiasis, ringworm, dengue, chikungunya
questions.question: Which of the following statements about human diseases are correct?

statements.A: Plasmodium falciparum causes the most serious, malignant form of malaria.
statements.B: Rhinoviruses infect the nose and respiratory passage but not the lungs.
statements.C: Dengue and chikungunya are protozoan diseases spread by Anopheles mosquitoes.
statements.D: In pneumonia, the alveoli fill with fluid, and the lips and fingernails may turn grey to bluish.
statements.E: Entamoeba histolytica lives in the small intestine of humans.

solution.key_concept: Recall the pathogen, vector and site of infection for each disease.
steps: A is correct: P. falciparum causes malignant malaria.
B is correct: common cold does not affect the lungs.
C is incorrect: dengue and chikungunya are viral and spread by Aedes.
D is correct: these are signs of pneumonia.
E is incorrect: Entamoeba histolytica lives in the large intestine.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 3 and 4 each include C or E, both of which are false.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the vectors Aedes and Anopheles, or the small and large intestine.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Basic concepts of immunology and vaccines
questions.question: Which antibody crosses the placenta from mother to foetus?

solution.key_concept: Placental IgG gives the foetus passive immunity.
steps: IgG crosses the placenta.
IgA is abundant in colostrum, IgE mediates allergy, and IgM is the largest antibody (a pentamer).
solution.final_answer: Option (1): IgG
solution.why_not_others: IgA reaches the infant through colostrum, not the placenta. IgE is involved in allergy. IgM is too large to cross the placenta.
solution.common_trap: Confusing placental IgG with colostral IgA.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Basic concepts of immunology and vaccines
questions.question: Which of the following is a primary lymphoid organ?

solution.key_concept: Primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow and thymus) are where lymphocytes form and mature.
steps: Bone marrow and thymus are the primary lymphoid organs.
Spleen, tonsils and Peyer's patches are secondary lymphoid organs.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Thymus
solution.why_not_others: Spleen, tonsils and Peyer's patches are all secondary lymphoid organs.
solution.common_trap: Calling the large, blood-filtering spleen a primary organ.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Basic concepts of immunology and vaccines
questions.question: Which of the following gives a person passive immunity?
options: Hepatitis B vaccine produced in yeast
A booster dose of a vaccine

solution.key_concept: Passive immunity comes from ready-made antibodies. Active immunity comes from the body's own response to antigens.
steps: Antivenom contains preformed antibodies, so it gives quick, passive immunity.
Vaccines (including boosters) and infections make the body produce its own antibodies, which is active immunity.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Antivenom injected after a snakebite
solution.why_not_others: The vaccine, the booster dose and recovery from infection all stimulate the body's own antibody response, so they give active immunity.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that anything injected gives passive immunity. Vaccines give active immunity.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Basic concepts of immunology and vaccines
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: A second encounter with the same pathogen produces a stronger and faster immune response than the first encounter.
statements.R: The first encounter with a pathogen generates memory B and T cells.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Acquired immunity has memory, which produces the secondary (anamnestic) response.
steps: A is true: the secondary response is stronger and faster than the low-intensity primary response.
R is true: memory cells form after the first exposure. Vaccines work on the same principle.
These memory cells are the reason the second response is faster and stronger, so R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true and directly linked, which rules out options 2, 3 and 4.
solution.common_trap: Thinking the primary response is the stronger one.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Basic concepts of immunology and vaccines
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Cell-mediated immunity, which is responsible for graft rejection, is provided by B-lymphocytes.
statements.II: Allergy is an exaggerated IgG response in which mast cells release histamine and serotonin.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: T-lymphocytes give cell-mediated immunity. IgE mediates allergy.
steps: Statement I is incorrect: cell-mediated immunity comes from T-lymphocytes, while B-lymphocytes give humoral immunity.
Statement II is incorrect: allergy is an exaggerated IgE response, not an IgG response.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains one wrong term (B instead of T, and IgG instead of IgE), so neither statement is correct.
solution.common_trap: Accepting statement II because the histamine and serotonin part is correct.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cancer
questions.question: Cancer cells divide uncontrollably because they have lost

solution.key_concept: Normal cells stop dividing when they touch other cells, a property called contact inhibition.
steps: Cancer cells lose contact inhibition.
They keep dividing and form tumours.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): contact inhibition
solution.why_not_others: Cancer cells clearly keep the ability to divide, and they still respire and make proteins.
solution.common_trap: Thinking cancer is a gain of division ability rather than a loss of the control on division.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cancer
questions.question: Which of the following is a non-ionising radiation that acts as a carcinogen?

solution.key_concept: Carcinogenic radiation can be ionising or non-ionising.
steps: X-rays and gamma rays are ionising carcinogens.
UV radiation is a non-ionising carcinogen.
CT scans use X-rays, which are ionising.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): UV radiation
solution.why_not_others: X-rays, gamma rays and the X-rays used in CT scans are all ionising radiations.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting that CT relies on X-rays, which are ionising.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cancer
questions.question: Which technique for detecting cancer uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation?

solution.key_concept: MRI uses strong magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation.
steps: Radiography and CT both use X-rays.
Biopsy is the removal of tissue for histopathological study, not an imaging method.
MRI uses magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): MRI
solution.why_not_others: Radiography and CT use ionising X-rays. Biopsy is not an imaging technique.
solution.common_trap: Confusing CT (X-rays, 3-D images) with MRI (magnetic fields).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cancer
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Biological response modifier that activates the immune system against tumours

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Cellular genes that can be activated to transform cells

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Tissue sample taken for histopathological study

solution.key_concept: Cancer detection methods, treatments and oncogenes each have a distinct role.
steps: Alpha-interferon is a biological response modifier (A-II).
Biopsy is followed by histopathological study (B-IV).
CT uses X-rays to produce 3-D images (C-I).
Proto-oncogenes (c-onc) can be activated to transform cells (D-III).
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps the matches for interferon and biopsy. Option 2 swaps the matches for CT and proto-oncogenes. Option 4 swaps the matches for interferon and proto-oncogenes.
solution.common_trap: Linking interferon to genes instead of to immunotherapy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Cancer
questions.question: Which of the following statements about cancer are correct?

statements.A: Benign tumours invade surrounding tissues and metastasise.
statements.B: Leukaemia is detected by blood and bone marrow tests.
statements.D: Chemotherapy can cause side effects such as hair loss and anaemia.
statements.E: MRI uses X-rays to produce images of internal organs.

solution.key_concept: Know the tumour types, detection methods and treatment side effects.
steps: A is incorrect: benign tumours stay localised. Only malignant tumours invade and metastasise.
B is correct: leukaemia is detected by blood and bone marrow tests.
C is correct: oncogenic viruses carry viral oncogenes.
D is correct: chemotherapy can cause hair loss and anaemia.
E is incorrect: MRI uses magnetic fields and non-ionising radiation, while CT uses X-rays.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): B, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 4 each include A or E, both of which are false.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the properties of benign and malignant tumours, or of MRI and CT.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: HIV and AIDS
questions.question: Which enzyme of HIV copies its RNA genome into DNA that then integrates into the host genome?

solution.key_concept: HIV is a retrovirus. Its genetic information flows from RNA to DNA through reverse transcriptase.
steps: HIV has an RNA genome inside an envelope.
Inside the macrophage, reverse transcriptase makes a DNA copy of the viral RNA ($RNA \rightarrow DNA$).
This viral DNA integrates into the host DNA.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Reverse transcriptase
solution.why_not_others: RNA polymerase makes RNA from DNA, which is the opposite direction. DNA ligase only joins DNA fragments. Restriction endonuclease cuts DNA at specific sites.
solution.common_trap: Picking RNA polymerase simply because the genome is RNA.
solution.time_saving_tip: Retro means backward, so the enzyme is reverse transcriptase.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: HIV and AIDS
questions.question: After HIV enters the human body, which cells first act as the 'HIV factory'?

solution.key_concept: HIV first multiplies in macrophages. It later enters and destroys helper T cells.
steps: The virus first infects macrophages.
Its DNA copy integrates into the macrophage DNA, so the macrophage keeps producing virus particles.
The macrophage is therefore called the HIV factory.
HIV then enters helper T cells and destroys them.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Macrophages
solution.why_not_others: Helper T cells are the main cells killed, but they are not the HIV factory. The notes do not describe B-lymphocytes or RBCs as HIV factories.
solution.common_trap: Assuming HIV first infects helper T cells.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: HIV and AIDS
questions.question: Which of the following does NOT transmit HIV from an infected person?
options: Shaking hands with and hugging the infected person
Sharing injection needles with the infected person
Transfusion of blood donated by the infected person
Passage from an infected mother to her child through the placenta

solution.key_concept: HIV spreads only through body fluids, not by touch or physical contact.
steps: The listed routes of spread are sexual contact, contaminated blood, shared needles and the placenta.
Shaking hands and hugging involve no exchange of body fluids.
So casual contact does not transmit HIV.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Shaking hands with and hugging the infected person
solution.why_not_others: Shared needles, blood transfusion and placental transfer are all established routes of HIV transmission.
solution.common_trap: Believing that HIV spreads by casual physical contact.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: HIV and AIDS
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: AIDS patients commonly suffer from opportunistic infections caused by organisms such as Mycobacterium, fungi and Toxoplasma.
statements.R: HIV replicates in helper T-lymphocytes and destroys them, progressively lowering their number and making the person immunodeficient.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Loss of helper T cells causes immunodeficiency, which allows opportunistic infections.
steps: A is true: AIDS patients get infections by Mycobacterium, viruses, fungi and Toxoplasma.
R is true: HIV destroys helper T cells, so the TH count keeps falling.
With fewer helper T cells the immune system fails, and these infections take hold. So R explains A.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are factually correct, and R gives the direct cause of A, so options (2), (3) and (4) do not fit.
solution.common_trap: Thinking HIV itself causes these infections, rather than the loss of immunity it produces.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: HIV and AIDS
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The time lag between HIV infection and the appearance of AIDS symptoms may range from 5 to 10 years.
statements.II: After entering the body, HIV first infects helper T-lymphocytes, which then serve as the 'HIV factory'.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: AIDS has an incubation period of 5-10 years, and macrophages are the HIV factory.
steps: Statement I is correct: the period between infection and AIDS symptoms is 5-10 years.
Statement II is incorrect: HIV first infects macrophages, which become the HIV factory.
Helper T cells are infected later and are destroyed.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II reverses the sequence of infection, so options (1) and (4) are wrong. Statement I is true, so option (2) is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assuming helper T cells are the first cells HIV infects.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Adolescence; drug, alcohol and tobacco abuse
questions.question: Heroin (smack) is obtained by
options: extraction from the leaves of Cannabis sativa
processing of the leaves of Erythroxylum coca

solution.key_concept: Heroin is diacetylmorphine, made by acetylating morphine from Papaver somniferum.
steps: Morphine comes from the latex of the poppy Papaver somniferum.
Adding acetyl groups to morphine gives diacetylmorphine, which is heroin.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): acetylation of morphine
solution.why_not_others: Methylation is the wrong chemical change. Cannabis sativa gives cannabinoids, and Erythroxylum coca gives cocaine.
solution.common_trap: Confusing acetylation with methylation.
solution.time_saving_tip: The name diacetylmorphine itself tells you the process is acetylation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Adolescence; drug, alcohol and tobacco abuse
questions.question: Cocaine acts as a central nervous system stimulant by interfering with the transport of the neurotransmitter

solution.key_concept: Cocaine from Erythroxylum coca interferes with dopamine transport.
steps: Cocaine disturbs dopamine transport.
This stimulates the CNS and produces euphoria and increased energy.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): dopamine
solution.why_not_others: Cocaine's action is described in terms of dopamine transport, not acetylcholine, serotonin or GABA.
solution.common_trap: Picking another familiar neurotransmitter.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Adolescence; drug, alcohol and tobacco abuse
questions.question: In smokers, the amount of oxygen carried by haemoglobin decreases mainly because of a rise in the blood level of

solution.key_concept: Smoking raises blood carbon monoxide, which reduces the oxygen carried by haemoglobin.
steps: Tobacco smoke raises the CO level in the blood.
Higher CO reduces the oxygen carried by haemoglobin.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): carbon monoxide
solution.why_not_others: Nicotine stimulates the adrenal gland to release adrenaline and noradrenaline. These raise blood pressure and heart rate but do not reduce oxygen carriage by haemoglobin.
solution.common_trap: Blaming nicotine for every effect of smoking.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Adolescence; drug, alcohol and tobacco abuse
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Stimulates adrenal gland to release adrenaline and noradrenaline

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Depressant that slows down body functions

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Act on brain receptors and affect the cardiovascular system

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Interferes with dopamine transport, causing euphoria

solution.key_concept: Each drug has a characteristic action.
steps: Heroin is an opioid and a depressant: A-II.
Cocaine interferes with dopamine transport: B-IV.
Cannabinoids act on cannabinoid receptors in the brain and affect the cardiovascular system: C-III.
Nicotine stimulates the adrenal gland to release adrenaline and noradrenaline: D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) wrongly calls heroin the dopamine-acting stimulant. Option (3) swaps cocaine and cannabinoids. Option (4) swaps heroin and nicotine.
solution.common_trap: Calling heroin a stimulant.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fix A-II first, since heroin is a depressant. That eliminates options (1) and (4).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Adolescence; drug, alcohol and tobacco abuse
questions.question: Which of the following statements about drug and alcohol abuse are correct?

statements.A: Misuse of anabolic steroids by females can cause enlargement of the clitoris and deepening of the voice.
statements.B: Misuse of anabolic steroids by males can cause breast enlargement and reduced sperm production.
statements.C: Chronic use of alcohol damages the liver and can lead to cirrhosis.
statements.D: Morphine is a stimulant obtained from Erythroxylum coca.
statements.E: Misuse of anabolic steroids by males increases the size of the testicles.

solution.key_concept: Effects of anabolic steroids, alcohol and opioids.
steps: A is true: steroid misuse masculinises females, enlarging the clitoris and deepening the voice.
B is true: in males it causes breast enlargement and reduced sperm.
C is true: chronic alcohol use causes liver cirrhosis.
D is false: morphine comes from Papaver somniferum and is a sedative, not a stimulant.
E is false: steroid misuse reduces testicle size.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and C only
solution.why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) each include the false statement D or E.
solution.common_trap: Thinking steroids enlarge the testes, when they actually shrink them.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting D and E leaves only option (1).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in household food processing and industrial production
questions.question: The large holes in Swiss cheese are due to the production of a large amount of $CO_2$ by

solution.key_concept: Propionibacterium sharmanii produces a lot of $CO_2$ in Swiss cheese.
steps: Swiss cheese has large holes.
These holes come from the large amount of $CO_2$ produced by Propionibacterium sharmanii.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Propionibacterium sharmanii
solution.why_not_others: Lactobacillus makes curd. Yeast leavens dough. Aspergillus niger produces citric acid.
solution.common_trap: Choosing yeast because it is linked with $CO_2$ in bread.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in household food processing and industrial production
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of organic acid and the microbe producing it is correctly matched?

solution.key_concept: Microbial sources of organic acids.
steps: Citric acid is produced by Aspergillus niger.
Acetic acid is produced by Acetobacter aceti.
Butyric acid is produced by Clostridium butylicum.
Lactic acid is produced by Lactobacillus.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Butyric acid - Clostridium butylicum
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (2) swap the sources of citric and acetic acid. Lactobacillus produces lactic acid, not butyric acid.
solution.common_trap: Swapping Aspergillus and Acetobacter.
solution.time_saving_tip: Butylicum matches butyric, and aceti matches acetic.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in household food processing and industrial production
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes statins?
options: Produced by Trichoderma polysporum; used as immunosuppressants in organ transplants
Produced by Streptococcus; used to dissolve blood clots
Produced by Aspergillus niger; competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase
Produced by Monascus purpureus; competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase

solution.key_concept: Statins come from the yeast Monascus purpureus and lower cholesterol by competitively inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase.
steps: The source of statins is Monascus purpureus.
They competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme for cholesterol synthesis.
This lowers blood cholesterol.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Produced by Monascus purpureus; competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) describes cyclosporin A. Option (2) describes streptokinase. Option (3) gives the correct action but the wrong source, since Aspergillus niger makes citric acid.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the sources of statins and cyclosporin A.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in household food processing and industrial production
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Wine and beer are produced by fermentation of the broth followed by distillation.
statements.R: Whisky, brandy and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Wine and beer are made without distillation. Whisky, brandy and rum are distilled.
steps: Brewer's yeast ferments malted cereals and fruit juices.
Wine and beer are produced without distillation, so A is false.
Whisky, brandy and rum are produced with distillation, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options (1), (2) and (3) cannot be correct.
solution.common_trap: Believing that wine and beer are distilled.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in household food processing and industrial production
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Lactic acid bacteria increase the vitamin B12 content of curd and help check disease-causing microbes in the stomach.
statements.II: Cyclosporin A, used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ transplant patients, is obtained from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Benefits of lactic acid bacteria and the source of cyclosporin A.
steps: Statement I is correct: LAB increase vitamin B12 and check disease-causing microbes in the stomach.
Statement II is correct: cyclosporin A comes from Trichoderma polysporum and is an immunosuppressant.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the notes, so options (2), (3) and (4) are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Assigning cyclosporin A to Monascus purpureus, which is actually the source of statins.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in sewage treatment and energy generation
questions.question: Primary treatment of sewage in a sewage treatment plant involves
options: growth of aerobic flocs in aeration tanks
anaerobic digestion of sludge to produce biogas
formation of activated sludge in settling tanks
removal of debris by filtration and grit by sedimentation

solution.key_concept: Primary treatment is physical.
steps: Debris is removed by sequential filtration.
Grit is removed by sedimentation.
The settled solids form the primary sludge.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): removal of debris by filtration and grit by sedimentation
solution.why_not_others: Options (1), (2) and (3) are biological steps that occur during or after secondary treatment.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the steps of primary and secondary treatment.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in sewage treatment and energy generation
questions.question: The flocs formed during secondary treatment of sewage are
options: masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments forming mesh-like structures
masses of anaerobic methanogens that produce biogas in aeration tanks
aggregates of grit and debris settled at the bottom of the tank
solid particles left behind after filtration of sewage

solution.key_concept: Flocs are aerobic microbial masses that consume organic matter.
steps: Vigorous aeration allows aerobic microbes to grow as flocs.
A floc is a mass of bacteria associated with fungal filaments in a mesh-like structure.
Flocs consume organic matter and reduce BOD.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments forming mesh-like structures
solution.why_not_others: Methanogens are anaerobic and work in sludge digesters, not aeration tanks. Grit and debris are removed during primary treatment.
solution.common_trap: Thinking anaerobes act in the aeration tank.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in sewage treatment and energy generation
questions.question: Water sample X has a much higher BOD than water sample Y. This indicates that
options: X has lower organic pollution than Y
secondary treatment has been more effective on X than on Y
microbes need less oxygen to oxidise the organic matter in X
X has greater polluting potential than Y

solution.key_concept: BOD is an index of organic pollution.
steps: BOD is the oxygen microbes need to oxidise the organic matter in one litre of water.
A higher BOD means more organic matter is present.
So X is more polluted than Y.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): X has greater polluting potential than Y
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (3) reverse the meaning of BOD. Secondary treatment lowers BOD, so X has been treated less effectively, not more.
solution.common_trap: Assuming a low BOD means polluted water.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in sewage treatment and energy generation
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: II
list_II.text: Solids settled during sedimentation in primary treatment

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Sedimented flocs, partly returned to aeration tank as inoculum

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Methanogen also found in the rumen of cattle

solution.key_concept: Products and organisms of sewage treatment and biogas production.
steps: Primary sludge is the solid settled in primary treatment: A-II.
Activated sludge is the sedimented flocs, part of which is recycled as inoculum: B-III.
Methanobacterium is a methanogen found in the cattle rumen: C-IV.
Treated effluent is released into rivers and streams: D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps primary and activated sludge. Option (2) swaps C and D. Option (4) swaps A and C.
solution.common_trap: Confusing primary sludge with activated sludge.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes in sewage treatment and energy generation
questions.question: Which of the following statements about sewage treatment and biogas are correct?

statements.A: All of the activated sludge is pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters.
statements.B: Biogas contains mainly methane, along with $CO_2$, $H_2S$ and $H_2$.
statements.C: Biogas technology in India was developed mainly by IARI and KVIC.
statements.D: The Ganga Action Plan was launched by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to treat sewage before it reaches the river.
statements.E: Secondary treatment of sewage aims to increase the BOD of the effluent.

solution.key_concept: Fate of activated sludge, biogas composition and government initiatives.
steps: A is false: a small part of the activated sludge is returned to the aeration tank as inoculum, and only the rest goes to digesters.
B is true: biogas is mostly methane, with $CO_2$, $H_2S$ and $H_2$.
C is true: IARI and KVIC developed biogas technology in India.
D is true: the Ministry of Environment and Forests launched the Ganga Action Plan.
E is false: secondary treatment reduces BOD.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): B, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (3) include the false statement A, and option (2) includes the false statement E.
solution.common_trap: Forgetting that part of the activated sludge is recycled as inoculum.
solution.time_saving_tip: Rejecting A and E leaves only option (4).

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers
questions.question: Which of the following organisms forms a mycorrhizal association that mainly helps the plant absorb phosphorus from the soil?

solution.key_concept: Mycorrhiza is a fungal association, for example Glomus, that helps plants absorb phosphorus from soil.
steps: Phosphorus uptake from soil is the main role of mycorrhiza.
Glomus is the standard example of a mycorrhizal fungus.
Rhizobium, Azotobacter and Anabaena are nitrogen fixers, not phosphorus absorbers.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Glomus
solution.why_not_others: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in legume root nodules. Azotobacter is a free-living soil nitrogen fixer. Anabaena is a cyanobacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every biofertilizer works by fixing nitrogen. Mycorrhiza enriches the plant's nutrition mainly through phosphorus uptake.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the pairing: fungus (Glomus) goes with phosphorus, and bacteria or cyanobacteria go with nitrogen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers
questions.question: Baculoviruses are considered especially suitable for integrated pest management in ecologically sensitive areas because they
options: are species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal agents that do not harm non-target organisms
are broad-spectrum agents that kill all insects and arthropods present in the area
fix atmospheric nitrogen and thereby enrich the soil
are free-living fungi of root ecosystems that suppress plant pathogens

solution.key_concept: Baculoviruses, mainly the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus, attack insects and arthropods. They are species-specific and narrow-spectrum.
steps: Baculoviruses act as biological agents against insects and arthropods.
They are species-specific and have a narrow spectrum of action.
So non-target organisms are not harmed, which suits IPM in ecologically sensitive areas.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): are species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal agents that do not harm non-target organisms
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 contradicts their narrow-spectrum nature. Option 3 describes nitrogen-fixing biofertilizers. Option 4 describes Trichoderma.
solution.common_trap: Thinking a good biocontrol agent must kill as many pests as possible. In sensitive areas, specificity is the key advantage.
solution.time_saving_tip: Ecologically sensitive area means you should look for the words species-specific or narrow-spectrum.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers
questions.question: Spores of Bacillus thuringiensis sprayed on plants control butterfly caterpillars because
options: a toxin released in the larval gut after the spores are eaten kills the larvae, while other insects remain unharmed
the spores release a toxin on the leaf surface that kills every insect landing on the plant
the spores attack the caterpillar from outside its body without being ingested
the spores grow into fungal hyphae that invade and digest the caterpillars

solution.key_concept: Bt spores are eaten by caterpillars. A toxin released in the larval gut kills the larvae and leaves other insects unharmed.
steps: Caterpillars feeding on sprayed plants eat the Bt spores.
A toxin is released inside the larval gut.
The toxin kills the larvae, and other insects are not affected.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): a toxin released in the larval gut after the spores are eaten kills the larvae, while other insects remain unharmed
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 wrongly makes the toxin non-selective and places its action on the leaf surface. Option 3 ignores the fact that the spores must be ingested. Option 4 treats Bt as a fungus, but it is a bacterium.
solution.common_trap: Believing that Bt kills all insects. Its toxin acts in the larval gut, and other insects are spared.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Azotobacter fixes atmospheric nitrogen only within the root nodules of leguminous plants.
statements.R: Azotobacter is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium found in the soil.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen symbiotically in legume root nodules. Azotobacter and Azospirillum are free-living soil nitrogen fixers.
steps: Root-nodule nitrogen fixation in legumes is the role of Rhizobium, so A is false.
Azotobacter is free-living in soil and fixes nitrogen there, so R is true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3 cannot be correct, because each of them requires A to be true.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up Rhizobium (symbiotic, in root nodules) with Azotobacter (free-living).
solution.time_saving_tip: If A is false, only the option 'A is false but R is true' is left to check.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Microbes as biocontrol agents and biofertilizers
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc and Oscillatoria fix atmospheric nitrogen, act as important biofertilizers in paddy fields and also add organic matter to the soil.
statements.II: Apart from helping in phosphorus absorption, mycorrhizal plants show resistance to root-borne pathogens and tolerance to salinity and drought.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Cyanobacteria are nitrogen-fixing biofertilizers in paddy fields. Mycorrhiza gives phosphorus uptake, resistance to root pathogens, and tolerance to salinity and drought.
steps: Anabaena, Nostoc and Oscillatoria are cyanobacteria that fix $N_2$.
They are important biofertilizers in paddy fields and add organic matter, so Statement I is correct.
Mycorrhizal plants absorb phosphorus better.
They also resist root-borne pathogens and tolerate salinity and drought, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so any option that marks either statement as incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Doubting Oscillatoria as a nitrogen fixer, or limiting mycorrhiza to phosphorus uptake and forgetting its protective benefits.
